A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
H9N2 is an avian influenza virus that has been circulating in China for many years and has recently been found to infect humans.
the H9N2 influenza virus infection in mice can induce cross-protective immunity against the heterologous challenge.

H9N2 influenza virus infection induces protective immunity against homologous challenge, but not against heterologous virus challenge, and that vaccination with inactivated H9N2 whole virus vaccine is an efficacious strategy to prevent disease caused by H9N2 infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current vaccine is not effective against the H9N2 strain that was circulating in the human population.
vaccination with an H9N2 vaccine that contains the G1 HA can induce protection from challenge with H9N2 strains of both G1 and G2 subtypes.
vaccination with an inactivated whole virus vaccine can protect against infection by a heterologous virus in the absence detectable cross-reacting serum antibodies.
